title: Bash High-Performance Streaming Log Aggregator
description: Implement a high-throughput Bash pipeline that parses structured HTTP access logs from stdin, filters 5xx status codes, and outputs summary metrics.
prompt:
You are an expert Unix CLI systems engineer. Implement a Bash function `aggregate_logs()`:

Requirements:
1. Read log lines from stdin formatted as: `<timestamp> <status_code> <path> <latency_ms>`
2. Output two lines:
   - `5xx_COUNT=<total count of status codes >= 500>`
   - `MAX_LATENCY=<maximum latency_ms seen>`
3. Use `set -euo pipefail` and efficient `awk` processing.
4. Output ONLY the bash script in a markdown block.
test_code:
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DATA="2026-08-15 200 /api/v1/user 45
2026-08-15 500 /api/v1/checkout 320
2026-08-15 503 /api/v1/pay 1500
2026-08-15 200 /api/v1/health 12"

OUTPUT=$(echo "$LOG_DATA" | aggregate_logs)

echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "5xx_COUNT=2" || exit 1
echo "$OUTPUT" | grep -q "MAX_LATENCY=1500" || exit 1

echo "Bash Log Aggregator Test Passed!"
